long_biography.plain_text:
McLeod entered the landscape-materials trade through a practical problem at home. Unable to find someone to place boulders, he and Michelle bought stone and an old crane, then accepted small setting jobs while raising two children. He operated the crane as she handled customer enquiries, and the couple turned that modest start into Southwest Boulder & Stone.

Under McLeod's ownership, the company developed a chain of Southern California yards serving commercial and residential buyers. Its catalogue grew across boulders, aggregates, flagstone, masonry products and fabricated stone, supported by delivery, placement and product guidance. He also helped rethink the traditional open rock yard, including warehouse-based layouts that brought large natural-stone displays closer to urban customers. The enduring model combines hands-on selection, practical education and drought-conscious landscaping materials for contractors, designers and homeowners.
